record.context_brief: Endpoint commutator spaces for H-system data
record.original_question: Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, let u ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n, R^{n+1}), and set b = H(u) ∈ W^{1,n}(R^n) ∩ L^∞(R^n). Determine the largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(R^n) for which the commutator [b, I] maps V to L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n) or to W^{1,1}(R^n), the commutators [b, R_α] map V to L^1(R^n), the Jacobian form du^1 ∧ ... ∧ du^n admits an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, and whether the answers change when u is assumed to solve an H-system.

evidence.quote: Problem 4.1. Fix H bounded and Lipschitz on R^{n+1}, and u ∈ W1,n(R^n, R^{n+1}), so that b = H(u) ∈ W1,n(R^n) ∩ L∞(R^n). (a) What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1(R^n) such that [b, I]: V -> L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n)? What is the answer if we replace L^{n/(n-1)}(R^n) by W1,1(R^n)? Does this V contain the n × n minors of Du?

(b) What is the largest subspace V ⊂ H1(R^n) such that all commutators [b, Rα] of the multiplication by b with the Riesz transforms Rα, α = 1, . . . , n, map V -> L1(R^n)? Does V contain all the n × n minors of Du? (c) Does du1 ∧ . . . ∧ dun have an atomic decomposition into b-atoms, i.e. standard atoms that are, in addition, orthogonal to b? (d) Do the answers to the above questions change if u is not just an element of W1,n, but also a solution to an H-system?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 2. Let H : ℝ^{n+1} → ℝ be a bounded Lipschitz function, and let u ∈ W^{1,n}(ℝ^n, ℝ^{n+1}). Set
   b := H(u),
so that b ∈ W^{1,n}(ℝ^n) ∩ L^∞(ℝ^n).

Denote by H^1(ℝ^n) the real Hardy space, by I the identity operator, and by R_α (α = 1, …, n) the classical Riesz transforms. For a function b ∈ L^∞ and an operator T, the commutator [b, T] is defined by [b, T]f = b·Tf − T(bf). A "b-atom" means a standard H^1-atom a (supported in a ball B, with ‖a‖_∞ ≤ |B|^{−1} and ∫a = 0) which in addition satisfies ∫ a · b dx = 0.

Determine, with proof, the following:

(a) The largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(ℝ^n) such that the multiplication–commutator [b, I] : V → L^{n/(n−1)}(ℝ^n) is bounded. Same question with the target space replaced by the Sobolev space W^{1,1}(ℝ^n). In each case decide whether V contains all n × n minors of the Jacobian Du (in particular the form du^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du^n).

(b) The largest subspace V ⊂ H^1(ℝ^n) such that all the Riesz commutators [b, R_α] : V → L^1(ℝ^n) (α = 1, …, n) are bounded, and whether this V contains all n × n minors of Du.

(c) Whether the Jacobian form du^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ du^n always admits an atomic decomposition into b-atoms (in the sense above).

(d) Whether the answers to (a), (b), (c) change when u is additionally assumed to be a solution of an H-system, i.e. it satisfies
   Δu = 2 H(u) u_{x_1} ∧ ⋯ ∧ u_{x_n}   (in the appropriate weak sense for n-harmonic-type maps).
artifact.category_tag: Endpoint commutator and Hardy-space estimates for Jacobians
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches for endpoint commutator characterizations on Hardy spaces with H-system data, b-atom atomic decompositions of Jacobians, and related Riesz commutator endpoint mapping properties did not return any source resolving these specific questions. The questions appear to remain open, but no definitive recent reference confirming a solution (or its open status) was located.

status_evidence.title: Weak Factorizations of the Hardy Space H^1(R^n) in Terms of Multilinear Riesz Transforms
status_evidence.snippet: Weak factorization results for H^1 via Riesz commutators are developed but do not address the H-system / b-atom endpoint problems posed here.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature on Riesz commutators and H^1 does not resolve the specific largest-subspace / b-atom decomposition problems for Jacobians of W^{1,n} maps.
